name: Svinoriz 10 Opto
about: The Svinoriz 10 Opto's component spec (DRN-03; p5-drone task 1.2), written from docs/object-sheets/drone.md, letter T's frame, arms, packs and legs (D-043) and the pilot's simpler drone (D-050): the fiber coil in the class's canister beneath the frame, fore-aft on the centreline under the two packs, which run along the sides below the arms, tilted rear-down to its nozzle, the line's exit; a plain plastic bottle strapped rigidly on top, fore-aft, the only load, its filled mass the setup's additional weight; four plastic tube legs on two fore-aft skids of the same tube (rigid PVC-U after the pilot's 'plastic, a little soft', in T's shape and look; p7g-legs 1.1). legs_off is the legs-off build: legs, T-joints and skids off and every other part where it is; the drone lifts off the upside-down chair's posts under its arms, so the coil never touches the ground. The parts stand at the nominal in-flight loadout, a 1.0 kg bottle and the coil half paid out, 4.83 kg. Body frame of DetMath.cs: x right, y up, z forward, metres from the arm-plane centre. Nothing is balanced: the stack's forward offset puts the centre of mass about 0.5 mm forward (derived) and leaves a small product of inertia I_yz, and the mass build keeps both. Every number is labelled where it stands (pilot, measured, published, derived or assumed) and the note gives its source or its calculation; 'the sheet' is the object sheet, 'T' the reference letter.

fields.bootstrap: true for p6-flight-core's stand-in (now a test fixture); this researched file sets false
fields.parts: every rigid part the mass build sums (PHB-02): name (unique), kind (box | cylinder), material (carbon | aluminium | steel | polymer | li_ion | electronics), mass_kg (above 0), position_m (the part's centre); a box has size_m, its extents along body x, y, z; a cylinder is solid, with diameter_m, length_m and axis (the direction of its length, normalised when read). A part is a mass shape: its inertia, not its look (the props and arms say how they map)
fields.motors: four, in Betaflight's Quad X order (rear right, front right, rear left, front left): position_m (the prop hub, where the thrust acts), spin (cw | ccw seen from above; cw is a positive rotation about body +y), kv_rpm_per_v, resistance_ohm (the DC model's resistance: winding, ESC and leads), no_load_current_a (the bearings' and iron's loss, as the torque Kt·I0), rotor_inertia_kg_m2 (bell, shaft and prop about the shaft), magnet_poles, esc_tau_s (the ESC's command lag: the DShot frame, the PWM and the winding's L/R as one first-order lag), esc_current_limit_a (the ESC's current limit: the motor's current never passes it while the ESC drives; "none" for an ESC that senses no current), esc_disarm (what the ESC does with its spinning motor when the flight controller disarms: freewheel | blheli_s | blheli_s_brake_on_stop | bluejay | bluejay_brake_on_stop; a motor without it freewheels, the model before 42); the motor's lag τ_m = J/(Kt·Ke/R + ∂Q/∂ω) follows from these and the load; internals (p7f-damage design 8, 9; optional, on all four or none, every value with its note): bell_band_m (the turning bell's band, [from, to] m above the motor's base), can_thickness_m and can_yield_pa (the aluminium can), back_iron_thickness_m and back_iron_yield_pa (the steel ring behind the magnets), gap_m (magnets to stator), magnet_thickness_m, magnet_remanence_t (B_r) and magnet_relative_permeability (μ_r), shaft_diameter_m, shaft_yield_pa and shaft_ultimate_pa, hub_height_m (the prop's hub above the base: position_m over the motor part's base), bearing_heights_m ([lower, upper] above the base), and the bearings' bearing_static_rating_n (C0r), bearing_dynamic_rating_n (Cr), bearing_balls, bearing_ball_diameter_m and bearing_pitch_diameter_m; stator_band_m (the stator's laminations, [from, to] m above the base, where the magnets face it), stator_diameter_m, can_modulus_pa and back_iron_modulus_pa (p7f-damage 1.5: the bell as a ring and its rub)
fields.props: the four props, alike: diameter_m, blades, pitch_m (geometric, per revolution), k_t_n_per_rad2_s2 (T = k_T·n², n in rad/s) and kappa_m (Q = κ·T), both static at reference_rpm (one of static_rpm's points); static_rpm with static_thrust_ratio and static_torque_ratio (C_T and C_P there over their values at reference_rpm: the coefficients' change with rpm); inflow_advance_ratio (J = V_a/(n·D) of the axial inflow, from 0) with inflow_thrust_ratio and inflow_torque_ratio (C_T and C_P there over their static values); linear between points, held at the ends; h_force_n_per_m_s (the rotor's in-plane drag, the H-force, per m/s of its hub's in-plane airspeed at reference_rpm, growing in proportion to the rotor's speed); blade (p7f-damage design 1; optional, every value with its note): one blade as a structure, stations_r_over_r (equal spans' middles, r/R, the last span ending at the tip) with chord_m, thickness_m, section_angle_rad (the chord line's to the disc plane) and fill (section area over chord × thickness) at each; hub_diameter_m, hub_thickness_m and hub_bore_m (the hub, a cylinder less its bore); its material, moisture (dry | conditioned), density_kg_m3, flexural_modulus_pa, flexural_strength_pa, crush_strength_pa, fracture_energy_j_per_m2, proportional_limit (the share of the flexural strength past which a section keeps a set) and hardness_pa; the blades and the hub weigh the prop part ("prop_rr") within 0.1 g
fields.packs: two (PHB-03): part (the pack's mass part), series and parallel cells, cell_capacity_ah, r_cell_ohm, ocv_v (one cell's open-circuit voltage at states of charge 0, 1/(n−1), …, 1)
fields.legs: parts (the four leg parts, in Betaflight's corner order; a leg's length is its part's, its foot the part's lower end, where it meets level ground), stiffness_n_per_m and damping_n_s_per_m (each leg's own spring and damper, in series with the ground), foot_radius_m (the foot's curvature); tube, clamp and tjoint, what the legs are built of (p7g-legs 1.1): the legs' and skids' tube (material, outer and inner diameter, the free length between the clamp and the T-joint, the cracked stiffness factor, and the modulus, yield and ultimate stress, elongation at break and density, each with its published bounds as <name>_bounds: [min, max]), the clamp under each arm (its jaws' material and modulus, the grip length, the wing-nut bolt's diameter, the arm's give under it, and the hand's torque, the nut factor, the jaws' friction and the edge's stress factor with their bounds) and the T-joint on each skid (its material, socket diameter, the skid's grip length, the pinch screw's diameter and torque, and the print's interlayer strength); with them, every value of the block carries a note, its source; legs off is legs_off's build
fields.legs_off: the legs-off build (D-043, D-050): removed (every part that comes off with the legs, the four leg parts among them; they weigh 0 kg), moved ({part name: its labelled centre on the legs-off build}; D-050's layout moves none: the coil is beneath and the bottle on top on both builds); every other part stays as it is
fields.coil: part (the spool's mass part, the wound pack on its bobbin, whose mass falls as the line pays out; the canister round it is the canister part), housing (the part the pack rides in, the canister: its cylinder carries the coil's drag, as the pack inside is hidden, and it shares the pack's mount and play; optional), spool_mass_kg (the empty bobbin; its note gives the line's exit, the canister's nozzle tip), fiber_mass_kg and fiber_length_m (the line on a full spool); the part's mass here is this file's loadout
fields.payload: part (the payload's mass part, set to the pilot's payload: D-050's plain plastic bottle strapped rigidly on top, its filled mass the setting), mass_min_kg and mass_max_kg (the setting's range, APP-03); the part is the bottle at its mass here, this file's loadout; another payload scales it uniformly by the cube root of the mass ratio, growing away from the arm plane (its face toward the frame stays put), and 0 kg leaves it off
fields.camera: the FPV camera: lens_m (its lens, body m; the camera mount's point, where the modes and the body's turn give the feed its vibration and angular velocity, AirframeModesSpec.Camera, and where the feed's air velocity at the camera is taken for the lens drops, FEED-13, p7c-wind 1.7)
fields.stand: the legs-off launch stand (D-022, D-043): material, post_radius_m (each post on a motor diagonal, from the stand's centre), post_height_m (the post tops above the ground), post_diameter_m, mass_kg
fields.aero: the airframe's drag (p6-flight-core 1.5): air_density_kg_m3; body_area_m2 (the silhouette less the coil's, projected along body x, y and z: side, top, front); body_center_of_pressure_m (where the body's drag acts); drag_coefficient (of the body's silhouette and of the coil, whose own drag acts at the coil part's centre with its cylinder's silhouette)
fields.contacts: the contact model (p6-flight-core 1.6): margin_m (StaticContacts' margin), crash_accel_m_s2 (the crash threshold; a prop strike ends no flight since p7f-damage 1.3), impact_window_s and impact_speed_m_s (what an impact is), friction_stiffness_ratio, damping_mass_share, ground_friction_static and ground_friction_kinetic, ring_segments; shapes[]: name (unique), part (the mass part it belongs to: a part at 0 kg has no shapes, and a moved or scaled part moves or scales its shapes), role (support: a load-bearing sphere on a skid, on the ground and on objects, carried by its corner's leg spring; skid: a skid segment's capsule, on objects only, a contact within two radii of a touching support of its part dropped as the same support; body: a frame part on the ground and on objects, with its own stiffness_n_per_m (across body y), stiffness_up_n_per_m (along it; the same when absent) and damping_ratio; disc: a prop disc at its motor's hub, radius_m the flown prop's, half_thickness_m the blade's, strikes only), corner (rr | fr | rl | fl, for supports, skids and discs), material (carbon_composite | polymer | aluminium: the drone side of the contact), a_m (a sphere's centre or a capsule's core end), b_m (a capsule's other core end), radius_m

esc_tau_s.label: derived
esc_tau_s.note: p7b-airframe 1.0: the command's way from the flight controller to the motor's torque as one first-order lag, the sum of its delays (their first moment: within 0.1° of their phase below 60 Hz). The DShot300 frame, 53 µs (published: 16 bits at 300 kbit/s, sent every 250 µs, fc-profiles §1); the ESC takes the duty up at once (published sources: Bluejay sets its PWM registers in the frame's interrupt, AM32 in its 20 kHz loop, within 50 µs); the 24 kHz PWM's next period and its mean, about 42 µs (AM32's nominal 24 kHz, its source): about 0.1 ms in all (derived). Then the winding's current rise L/R, 0.3 ms (assumed, 0.1–0.6 ms: no inductance is published for these motors). The duty is not slewed: BLHeli_32's Maximum Acceleration (0.1–25.5 %/ms or maximum, its manual) is left at maximum, no limit, as ESC vendors advise; Bluejay has none (its source); AM32's ramp (16 %/ms above 40 k erpm, 6 below, 2 at start: its source) moves the filtered 200 °/s step by under 0.1 point and is left out. Design 5's 5 ms (assumed) gave that step 40.9 % overshoot (roll) against 29.2 % here; 0.2–0.7 ms gives 28.7–30.0 %

esc_current_limit_a.label: published
esc_current_limit_a.note: D-066, the class's published ESC: the Amaga / Vyriy 10 Opto build's SpeedyBee F405 V4 stack and its BLS 60A 4-in-1 (60 A a motor continuous, 80 A for 10 s, BLHeli_S J-H-50; fpv24.com, kiborg.com.ua), whose firmware senses no current and so limits none: BLHeli_S and Bluejay have no current limit, and BLHeli_32's current protection needs a sensing resistor and is off unless set. It replaces p6-flight-core 1.5's assumed policy, the motor's 40 A set as BLHeli_32's protection (D-051), kept as a variant (ShakeScenario.Protection). The firmware's one power limit, Bluejay's low-rpm protection (rpm power slope 9 by default, its source: the duty held to 9 × (255 div Comm_Period4x_H) of 255 below about 5000 rpm on these 7-pole-pair motors), acts only in the spin-up from idle and is left out (assumed). On a full pack the motor now draws 47.7 A at full duty, inside the ESC's 60 A, for 14.17 kgf in all (3.54 a motor: the published 3115 900 KV benches give 3.5–4.2 kgf a motor at full throttle on 6S, uav-en.tmotor.com, flyingtech.co.uk); 128 A for a few milliseconds of a spin-up from idle to full; the steady yaw authority at hover 831 °/s² and full yaw's first 50 ms 1959 °/s² (with 40 A protection 11.80 kgf and 1495 °/s²)

esc_disarm.label: published
esc_disarm.note: p6-flight-core 1.6c: the class's ESC is BLHeli_S J-H-50 (D-069). On a disarm Betaflight 4.5 sends DShot 0 to every ESC (dshot.c dshotInitEndpoints: *disarm = DSHOT_CMD_MOTOR_STOP; mixer.c: motor[i] = motor_disarmed[i] while not armed). BLHeli_S 16.7 at its defaults (bitdump/BLHeli, BLHeli_S SiLabs/BLHeli_S.asm: DEFAULT_PGM_BRAKE_ON_STOP 0; "Motor pwm is always damped light (aka complementary pwm, regenerative braking)") stays in its run loop at zero power: its PWM register at the minimum and the damping FET on for the rest of each period, so the active phases are shorted and the motor brakes as the DC model at d = 0. It leaves the loop when the commutation period passes 32 ms (about 1220 eRPM, run6_brake_done) or after 250 ticks of its 32 ms stop counter (8 s), and then turns every FET off (switch_power_off): the last 174 rpm coast. Bluejay 0.21, which the class's ESC may be flashed with (bird-sanctuary/bluejay: DEFAULT_PGM_BRAKE_ON_STOP 0, DEFAULT_PGM_BRAKING_STRENGTH 255), does the same down to about 1330 eRPM with no stop counter. Brake on stop, off in both, leaves the loop after 3 counter ticks and turns the three low-side FETs on (BLHeli_S after a 100 ms wait), kept as compared variants; G7's ESC-firmware question decides between them (pilot-questions.md)

bell_band_m.label: derived
bell_band_m.note: the bell, the motor's turning band, as heights above the motor's base (the arm top): from the stationary base's top, 6 mm (measured, T), to the can's top at the published 32 mm (Tarot and Flash Hobby Arthur 3115, Φ37.1 × 32 mm); a contact on the motor sphere between them is on the bell (design 8)

can_thickness_m.label: derived
can_thickness_m.note: the aluminium can's wall over the back iron: what the published radial room leaves, (37.2 − 31.0) / 2 = 3.1 mm from the stator's face (stator 31 × 15 mm, Flash Hobby Arthur 3115) to the can's outside (the motor part's Ø37.2 mm), after the gap, the magnet and the back iron (0.3 + 1.5 + 1.0 mm, assumed)

can_yield_pa.label: assumed
can_yield_pa.note: 6061-T6 aluminium's published yield, 276 MPa (ASM): the class's makers name 6061 or 7075 bells, 6061-T6 the softer and the commoner (assumed)

back_iron_thickness_m.label: assumed
back_iron_thickness_m.note: the steel ring behind the magnets that carries their flux: no maker of the class publishes it; 1.0 mm fits the published radial room with the gap and the magnet

back_iron_yield_pa.label: assumed
back_iron_yield_pa.note: a cold-drawn low-carbon steel ring: AISI 1018 cold drawn yields at 370 MPa, 1010 hot rolled at 180 MPa (published, ASM); 350 MPa taken

gap_m.label: assumed
gap_m.note: the air gap from the magnets' face to the stator's teeth, typical of the class (design 8: no maker publishes it)

magnet_thickness_m.label: assumed
magnet_thickness_m.note: l_m, the arc magnets' radial thickness (design 8: no maker publishes it)

magnet_remanence_t.label: published
magnet_remanence_t.note: B_r of sintered NdFeB N52H at 20 °C, the grade's 1.42–1.48 T (its standard grade tables); the class's 3115 900 KV 12N14P motors name N52H magnets (GEPRC EM3115, BrotherHobby SE 3115, Foxeer Black Hornet 3115)

magnet_relative_permeability.label: published
magnet_relative_permeability.note: μ_r, sintered NdFeB's recoil permeability, 1.03–1.10 (Hanselman 2006, Brushless Permanent Magnet Motor Design)

shaft_diameter_m.label: published
shaft_diameter_m.note: the 3115 class's 5 mm shaft (Tarot and Flash Hobby Arthur 3115, GEPRC EM3115, T-Motor Velox V3115); solid (design 9; Foxeer's 3115 is hollow)

shaft_yield_pa.label: assumed
shaft_yield_pa.note: no maker of the class publishes its shaft's steel: a quenched and tempered alloy steel, design 9's 1.2–1.8 GPa, its lower end

shaft_ultimate_pa.label: assumed
shaft_ultimate_pa.note: the same steel's tensile strength, 1.25 × its yield (assumed, a quenched and tempered alloy steel's ratio); the shaft breaks past it times the round section's plastic shape factor (design 9)

hub_height_m.label: derived
hub_height_m.note: the prop's hub above the motor's base: position_m's y, 0.035, less the base at 0.003 (the motor part's centre, 0.019, less half its 0.032 length)

bearing_heights_m.label: assumed
bearing_heights_m.note: the lower and upper bearings above the motor's base, 12 mm apart with the hub 16 mm above the upper one (design 9, from the motor's 32 mm height and its 15 mm stator); a strike's moment at the upper bearing and the two bearings' loads follow by statics

bearing_static_rating_n.label: published
bearing_static_rating_n.note: the 685ZZ's basic static load rating C0r (NMB's spec sheet; NSK 281 N): 5 × 11 × 5 mm, NSK or NMB, as the sheet and GEPRC EM3115 list

bearing_dynamic_rating_n.label: published
bearing_dynamic_rating_n.note: the 685ZZ's basic dynamic load rating Cr (NMB's spec sheet; NSK 790 N)

bearing_pitch_diameter_m.label: derived
bearing_pitch_diameter_m.note: the ball set's pitch circle, the mean of the 5 mm bore and the 11 mm outside (assumed equal); with D_w and the 8 balls it sets the ball-pass frequencies (design 9)

stator_band_m.label: assumed
stator_band_m.note: the stator's laminations as heights above the motor's base, its published 15 mm (stator 31 × 15 mm, Flash Hobby Arthur 3115) standing 2 mm above the bell's lower lip, the windings' end turns and the can's top above it (no maker publishes the stack's place); the magnets face it across the gap there, so a dent can narrow the gap only between these heights (p7f-damage 1.5)

stator_diameter_m.label: published
stator_diameter_m.note: the stator's 31 mm (Flash Hobby Arthur 3115, Tarot 3115: 31 × 15 mm, 12N14P); the can, the back iron, the magnet and the gap fill the motor part's 37.2 mm to it, and its teeth carry the magnets' rub

can_modulus_pa.label: published
can_modulus_pa.note: 6061-T6 aluminium's Young's modulus, 68.9 GPa (ASM), as can_yield_pa's alloy

back_iron_modulus_pa.label: published
back_iron_modulus_pa.note: a low-carbon steel's Young's modulus, 200 GPa (ASM, AISI 1010–1018), as back_iron_yield_pa's steel

diameter_m.label: measured
diameter_m.note: 10 inches: T measures 10.0–10.4 tip to tip at the 452 mm scale, the class's 10-inch (K§5.1)

pitch_m.label: assumed
pitch_m.note: 4.5 inches: the prop whose published table gives k_T and κ, inside the sheet's 10 × 4.5–5 class

k_t_n_per_rad2_s2.label: derived
k_t_n_per_rad2_s2.note: APC 10x4.5MR, 2-blade, its published static performance data (apcprop.com, PER3_10x45MR.dat, v2022-0915): 12.43 N at 9000 rpm, C_T 0.1079–0.1097 over 8000–12 000 rpm, so k_T = T/n² = 1.394–1.418e-5 there, 1.400e-5 at 9000 rpm, the hover (8800–9100 rpm at 4.8–5.2 kg). The table is APC's computation; the Flash Hobby 3115 900 KV bench (published) gives 1.55–1.69e-5 with its own 10 × 5 of unstated blade count, and UIUC's measured static C_T of 2-blade 10-inch APC props is 0.091–0.130 below 6700 rpm (m-selig.ae.illinois.edu)

kappa_m.label: derived
kappa_m.note: the same table's static torque over thrust: 0.01454 at 8000, 0.01443 at 9000 and 0.01436 m at 10 000 rpm (C_P 0.0387, κ = C_P·D/(2π·C_T)); below design 5's assumed 0.015–0.02, which was for a 3-blade: a 4.5-inch 2-blade turns less torque per newton, so yaw authority is a little weaker

reference_rpm.label: derived
reference_rpm.note: k_T and κ are the table's static values at 9000 rpm, the hover of 4.8–5.2 kg

static_rpm.label: published
static_rpm.note: the APC 10x4.5MR table's static rows (PER3_10x45MR.dat, v2022-0915)

static_thrust_ratio.label: derived
static_thrust_ratio.note: C_T over its 0.1083 at 9000 rpm: C_T rises from 0.106 at 1000 to 0.111 at 14 000 rpm (the blades' Reynolds number), which a constant k_T leaves out

static_torque_ratio.label: derived
static_torque_ratio.note: C_P over its 0.0387 at 9000 rpm: the drag torque per n² is 23 % higher at 1000 rpm (idle), 1–3 % between 6000 and 17 000

inflow_advance_ratio.label: published
inflow_advance_ratio.note: the same table at 9000 rpm, every second row to zero thrust at J 0.588 (linear between them within 0.06 % of C_T and 0.26 % of C_P)

inflow_thrust_ratio.label: derived
inflow_thrust_ratio.note: C_T(J) over the static C_T at 9000 rpm: APC's blade-element and momentum computation of the axial-inflow derate (PHB-03); the same ratios hold within 0.5 % from 4000 to 18 000 rpm

inflow_torque_ratio.label: derived
inflow_torque_ratio.note: C_P(J) over the static C_P at 9000 rpm: the torque falls more slowly than the thrust, so the inflow costs power as momentum theory says (within 2 % to J 0.3 from 4000 to 18 000 rpm, 5 % by J 0.5)

h_force_n_per_m_s.label: derived
h_force_n_per_m_s.note: p7c-wind 1.6 (PHY-17a), blade-element theory of a rigid 2-blade rotor, its in-plane force averaged over a turn: h = N_b·½ρ·[Ω·c_d0·∫c·r dr + ½·a·v_in·∫c·(β − α_L0) dr] (Johnson, Helicopter Theory: the profile term σc_d0μ/4 and the lift tilted by the inflow), with the sheet's chord (26 mm at 0.3 R tapering to 8 mm at the tip; 18 mm at 0.1 R assumed), β the 4.5-inch pitch's helix angle, a = 5.7 per rad (assumed), and α_L0 −6.3° and c_d0 0.049 fitted so the same elements give APC's published static 12.43 N and κ 0.0144 m at 9000 rpm. At the cruise (18.8 m/s at P's 22.7°: 10 050 rpm, 12.5 N a rotor, 12.0 m/s through the disc) it is 0.049 N per m/s, 0.008 of it the blades' profile drag and 0.041 their lift tilted by the inflow; over that rotor speed's 1.116 of the reference, 0.044 here (0.033 with the inboard sections' lift capped at stall, c_l 1.2). It replaces p6-flight-core 1.5's 0.225, tuned to fly P's pitch at 13 m/s: 5× a rigid rotor's, and with it P's pitch flies 13.0 m/s, below the published 17–22; and, at the merge with unity/main, p7b-airframe 1.7's 0.25, the same tuning on D-050's silhouette (13.0 m/s again). On D-050's silhouette P's 22.7° settles at 20.6 m/s with 0.044, inside 17–22; the element sums are the cruise's above. At the hover's 8800 rpm it is 0.036 s⁻¹ of rotor drag per unit mass, under the 0.1–0.4 s⁻¹ fitted on small quadrotors at low speed, which lump the body's drag and flexible blades' flapping that a stiff multirotor prop has little of (assumed)

stations_r_over_r.label: assumed
stations_r_over_r.note: p7f-damage design 1: the blade as 40 equal spans of 0.0225 R from 0.1 R (its root, outside the hub's 9.5 mm, 0.075 R) to the tip, each station its span's middle; 1.2 checks its tables against 160

chord_m.label: assumed
chord_m.note: the sheet's chord (docs/object-sheets/drone.md: 26 mm at 0.3 R, inside the class's published 22–30 mm near 0.3 R, tapering linearly to 8 mm at the tip; 18 mm at 0.1 R assumed) at each station's middle: the law the flapping's and the interference's 19 stations fly (DroneSpec.BuildFlapping), so the blade's elements keep p7c-wind 1.6's fit of α_L0 and c_d0 to APC's published static thrust and κ

thickness_m.label: derived
thickness_m.note: the section's greatest thickness: a thickness-to-chord law (assumed: 11 % at 0.3 R to 8 % at the tip, design 1; inboard of 0.3 R rising linearly to 20 % at 0.1 R, the root thickening into the 8 mm hub) scaled by 1.5026 so the two blades and the hub weigh the prop part's published 16 g: each blade 6.558 g (density × fill × chord × thickness over the spans), the hub 2.884 g (Ø19 × 8 mm less its 5 mm bore). Scaled, the blade is 16.5 % thick at 0.3 R (4.2 mm), 12 % at the tip (1.0 mm) and 5.4 mm at its root against the hub's 8 mm. Blades and hub turn 4.25e-5 kg·m² about the shaft (rotor_inertia_kg_m2's note: the prop about 4.7e-5)

section_angle_rad.label: derived
section_angle_rad.note: the chord line's angle to the disc plane: the 4.5-inch pitch's helix, atan(p / (2π·r)) with pitch_m, 52.2° at the root station, 10.8° at 0.75 R and 8.2° at the tip, as the flapping's elements; their zero-lift line lies α_L0 below it (−6.3°, RotorFlappingSpec.ZeroLiftAngle, p7c-wind 1.6's fit), added where the lift is computed (design 1's "helix less α_L0"); a new blade has no set

fill.label: derived
fill.note: the section's area over chord × thickness: 0.685 for the NACA four-digit thickness form (its published ordinates, Abbott and von Doenhoff 1959, integrated over the chord; camber moves no area), taken at every station (assumed: a prop's root is fuller, toward an ellipse's 0.785)

hub_diameter_m.label: assumed
hub_diameter_m.note: the sheet's hub, Ø19 mm, inside the class's published Ø18–20 mm

hub_thickness_m.label: published
hub_thickness_m.note: a 2-blade 10-inch nylon prop's hub is 6–9 mm thick (the sheet: Gemfan 1045 6 mm, a 3-blade 10 × 5 9 mm); 8 mm, as the prop part's length_m

hub_bore_m.label: published
hub_bore_m.note: the hub's bore is the 3115 class's 5 mm shaft (Tarot and Flash Hobby Arthur 3115, GEPRC EM3115)

moisture.label: assumed
moisture.note: the material values below are the conditioned column of BASF's data (the moisture equilibrium at 23 °C and 50 % relative humidity) rather than dry as moulded: nylon takes the air's water up after moulding, and the props are kept and flown in field air and in rain. Dry, the blade is stiffer and stronger (flexural modulus 9.27 against 6.5 GPa, flexural strength 293 against 205 MPa) and less tough (Charpy notched 10 against 13 kJ/m²)

density_kg_m3.label: published
density_kg_m3.note: PA66-GF30, the black glass-filled nylon of the sheet's props: BASF Ultramid A3WG6 LT BK, product information 09/2026, ISO 1183. Only the dry part's density is published; the water a conditioned blade holds would add about 1 % (assumed), and the thickness fit keeps the prop at its published 16 g whatever the density

flexural_modulus_pa.label: published
flexural_modulus_pa.note: BASF Ultramid A3WG6 LT BK, ISO 178, conditioned (9.27 GPa dry): the sections' elastic stiffness

flexural_strength_pa.label: published
flexural_strength_pa.note: σ_f, a section's fracture in bending (design 1): BASF Ultramid A3WG6 LT BK, ISO 178, conditioned (293 MPa dry; its stress at break in tension 127 MPa conditioned, 190 dry)

crush_strength_pa.label: assumed
crush_strength_pa.note: σ_c, the mean stress of a section crushed against a harder face: glass-filled PA66's published compressive stress at 5 % strain, 112 MPa (Ertalon 66 GF30, Mitsubishi Chemical Advanced Materials, ISO 604; 43 and 77 MPa at 1 and 2 %), and 117 MPa at 10 % (TECAMID 66 GF30, Ensinger, ASTM D695), dry stock shapes; taken for the conditioned moulded blade (assumed: its water lowers it, a strike's strain rate raises it). It is 0.55 σ_f, the order design 1 assumed

fracture_energy_j_per_m2.label: derived
fracture_energy_j_per_m2.note: G_c: BASF Ultramid A3WG6 LT BK's notched Charpy energy per ligament area (ISO 179/1eA), 13 kJ/m² conditioned at 23 °C (10 dry; 8.5 conditioned at −30 °C), taken as the work a section's fracture costs per area of its section (an upper estimate: the specimen's own kinetic and plastic work are in it)

proportional_limit.label: assumed
proportional_limit.note: the share of σ_f past which a section keeps a permanent set (design 1): glass-filled nylon is quasi-brittle, and conditioned it breaks at 6.5 % strain where its elastic line would reach the break stress at 1.9 % (BASF: 127 MPa over 6.8 GPa), so its curve bends well before the break; 0.7 is design 1's assumption, its sensitivity printed by 1.7

hardness_pa.label: published
hardness_pa.note: H_b, the blade's ball-indentation hardness (ISO 2039-1) for Rabinowicz's rule (design 5): PA66-GF30 165 MPa (Ertalon 66 GF30, Mitsubishi Chemical Advanced Materials) to 210 MPa (APSOplast PA 66 GF30), dry stock shapes; the lower taken for the conditioned blade, which water softens. Timber across the grain (tens of MPa) is softer, concrete, masonry and steel (GPa) harder

series.label: derived
series.note: 6S: the 3115 900 KV motors are rated 3–6S (published); the class's 8S (fc-profiles.md) would need about 900·6/8 = 675 KV, and at 8S these motors would draw about 80 A each at full throttle on this prop, twice their 40 A (derived)

parallel.label: derived
parallel.note: two identical packs (T, the pilot's 'a couple of batteries') in parallel make the pilot's 6S4P (pilot: 6S4P to 6S5P, 20–35 Ah): 20 Ah, 432 Wh, the one even arrangement inside 4P–5P; T's packs, two cells high and 0.22 m long, hold 12 cells each

cell_capacity_ah.label: published
cell_capacity_ah.note: Molicel INR21700-P50B: 5.0 Ah typical, 4.85 Ah minimum, 3.6 V, 2.5 V cut-off, 60 A continuous, 71 ± 1 g, Ø21.45 × 70.05 mm (akkuteile.de). 5 Ah makes 6S4P the pilot's 20 Ah (a 4.5 Ah P45B gives 18), and its 60 A covers the about 50 A a cell at full throttle in 4P (derived), which a 25 A Samsung 50S does not

r_cell_ohm.label: assumed
r_cell_ohm.note: under load, 1.5 × the P50B's published ≤ 8 mΩ at shipping (AC); the sheet's 12–16 mΩ, K§5.3's 15 mΩ; 1.4's sag scenario checks it

ocv_v.label: assumed
ocv_v.note: one cell at state of charge 0, 0.05, …, 1, over the P50B's published 5.0 Ah from its 4.2 V charge to its 2.5 V cut-off (published, akkuteile.de): the shape of the P50B's and like 5 Ah 21700 NMC cells' published low-rate discharge curves, read by shape and not digitised, so assumed; 3.40–4.07 V over 10–90 % (K§5.3: 3.4–4.1 V), the knee below 10 %: 4 V a unit of charge from 10 to 5 %, 14 V from 5 % to the cut-off (p7b-airframe 1.5; model 11's table stopped at 3.0 V, so the pack never emptied)

stiffness_n_per_m.label: derived
stiffness_n_per_m.note: p7g-legs 1.1, from the section (DroneLegs.VerticalStiffness): in series the tube's EA/L = 3.0e9 × 2.827e-5 / 0.2135 = 397 kN/m, the arm under the clamp bending out of its plane, 67.6 kN/m (clamp.mount_stiffness_n_per_m), and the skid's ring squeezed in the T-joint, 553 kN/m (the tube's ring over tjoint.skid_grip_length_m); the clamp's grip carries none of a push, since the tube's top bears on the arm's underside (leg_rr). Replaces the assumed 10 kN/m (model 26)

damping_n_s_per_m.label: derived
damping_n_s_per_m.note: ζ 0.2 (the sheet's 0.1–0.3, assumed) on a quarter of the file's 5.08 kg take-off mass (L5): c = 2ζ·√(k·m/4) = 2 × 0.2 × √(52300 × 1.27) = 103 N·s/m (was 45 on the assumed 10 kN/m)

foot_radius_m.label: measured
foot_radius_m.note: the skid tube's radius (T: Ø9–10 mm); the feet are skids, so each leg's foot is its T-joint on the skid

outer_diameter_m.label: measured
outer_diameter_m.note: T: Ø8–10 mm black tubes, the legs and the skids of one stock (the parts' diameter_m)

inner_diameter_m.label: published
inner_diameter_m.note: rigid PVC round tube is sold 10 mm OD × 8 mm ID (uxcell's rigid PVC pipe, 500 mm, white or dark grey high-impact): a 1 mm wall

free_length_m.label: derived
free_length_m.note: between the clamp's bottom (clamp_rr: y −0.01125 − 0.00825 = −0.0195) and the T-joint's top (tjoint_rr: −0.243 + 0.010 = −0.233)

cracked_stiffness_factor.label: assumed
cracked_stiffness_factor.note: design 3's half: a crack through about half the wall at the clamp's edge; no published value for a cracked PVC-U tube was found

loss_factor.label: published
loss_factor.note: rigid PVC's mechanical loss factor at room temperature: 0.028–0.040 in bending vibration near 1 kHz across the IUPAC working party's laboratories (Pure Appl. Chem. 35, 1973, 315; its torsion pendulum at 0.2–2 Hz on the same sheets), and under 0.02 for most rigid polymers (Plastics Technology's DMA notes); p7g-legs 1.2's side give damps at ζ = η/2, the tube's own, the jaws' and the T-joint's friction left out (a lower bound)

modulus_pa.label: published
modulus_pa.note: PVC-U, unplasticised rigid PVC (the pilot's 'plastic, a little soft'; T's smooth Ø10 mm tube, a stock rigid PVC size): Angst+Pfister's APSOplast PVC-U 00.001-01 technical data sheet (2024), 3000 N/mm² (DIN EN ISO 527); Reichelt Chemietechnik's PVC-U pressure pipe, 3000 MPa

modulus_bounds_pa.label: published
modulus_bounds_pa.note: APSOplast PVC-U 00.001-01 and 00.005-01 (3300 N/mm²), RCT's pipe (3000 MPa)

yield_stress_bounds_pa.label: published
yield_stress_bounds_pa.note: RCT's PVC-U pressure pipe 50 MPa, APSOplast PVC-U 00.005-01 58 N/mm²

ultimate_stress_pa.label: published
ultimate_stress_pa.note: APSOplast PVC-U 00.001-01's bending strength, 80 N/mm² (DIN EN ISO 178): the elastic-equivalent stress M·c/I at the most moment a bar carries, the stress design 3's fracture law compares

ultimate_stress_bounds_pa.label: derived
ultimate_stress_bounds_pa.note: 80 N/mm² scaled with the yield stress's published 50–58 over its 55 (one sheet gives the bending strength)

elongation_at_break.label: published
elongation_at_break.note: APSOplast PVC-U 00.001-01, 20 % (DIN EN ISO 527): ductile at 23 °C; notched Charpy 2–6 kJ/m² across the sheets and RCT's pipe (DIN EN ISO 179), so notch-sensitive; rated from −15 °C

modulus_pa.label: published
modulus_pa.note: the printed block's jaws: Prusament PETG technical data sheet v1.1 (2022), printed specimens, 1.5 ± 0.1 GPa (ISO 527-1); the class prints its clamps and T-joints (T: black printed blocks)

grip_length_m.label: derived
grip_length_m.note: the tube's length in the jaws: the clamp part's height (clamp_rr's size_m), the drone model's trim of T's 25 mm block

bolt_diameter_m.label: derived
bolt_diameter_m.note: M4: T's zinc-plated wing nut is 20 mm across the wings (the sheet), DIN 315's M4 (McMaster-Carr's DIN 315 listing: M4 20 mm, M5 26 mm; Würth's M5 26 mm)

mount_stiffness_n_per_m.label: derived
mount_stiffness_n_per_m.note: the 6 × 25 mm plate arm bending out of its plane under the clamp, 3EI/a³ with I = b·t³/12 and E 50 GPa (the arms' own contact derivation, arm_rr_a's stiffness_up_n_per_m), a = 0.145 − 0.045 = 0.100 m from the body's edge to the clamp at r 0.145

mount_side_stiffness_n_per_m.label: derived
mount_side_stiffness_n_per_m.note: p7g-legs (model 51): the same plate arm bending in its plane under the clamp, 3EI/a³ with I = t·b³/12 = 7.81e-9 m⁴ (b 25 mm, t 6 mm), E 50 GPa and the same a = 0.100 m (the arms' own in-plane derivation, arm_rr_a's stiffness_n_per_m); with mount_stiffness_n_per_m out of the plane it is a broken leg's stub's contact spring, the stub held in the clamp's jaws (no free tube left to give)

torque_n_m.label: published
torque_n_m.note: a hand's pinch torque on a 19 mm flange, tightening: 108.7 ± 16.1 in-oz, men (Imrhan and Munoz-Vasa 2013, 'Finger pinch loosening and tightening torques on small cylindrical handles', Industrial and Systems Engineering Review 1(2), Table 2); the 20 mm wing nut is pinched by its wings

torque_bounds_n_m.label: published
torque_bounds_n_m.note: the same mean ± 2 SD (0.768 ± 0.227 N·m); the paper's women reach 72 % of the men's

nut_factor.label: published
